We show how to fit stochastic epidemic models to many small and diverse outbreak datasets and apply the method to norovirus outbreaks, finding that the transmission rate is 0.0036 per infective-suspceptible day, the initial growth rate is 0,27 per infective day and outbreaks in long-term-care settings are significantly more transmissible.

(1) the generalized linear model framework can be used to estimate parameters from multiple small norovirus outbreak data; (2) the model can estimate initial growth rates in the outbreaks, allowing for characterization of the initial susceptible population or contact patterns in the outbreaks; and (3) the estimates of transmission rates and symptomatic periods from the model are robust to imputed missing infectious period data.
